title: Two full gates ran at once in luna-inbox despite [gate].max_parallel = 1 (default): one on the gated_at lease path, one background run
spec:
Evidence (luna-inbox, daemon pid 14714 on main 66d866c, 2026-10-09 11:58): two tests-green.sh processes started 2 s apart,
wt/T-0679 (pid 48288) and wt/T-0681 (pid 48700), both children of the daemon; load average reached 411 and swap 18.8 of 19.4 GB.
T-0679 pipeline gate keys: ['gate_attempts', 'gate_reds', 'gated_at', 'gated_at_lease'] gate_attempts=1; T-0681 pipeline gate keys: ['gate_attempts', 'gate_run_id', 'gate_started_at', 'gate_started_at_lease']. T-0679 had just finished a 52 min gate (its second attempt started at once); T-0681 started through the background gate
(gate_run_id, gate_started_at). The two paths do not share the max_parallel count. luna-inbox pool.toml [gate] does not set
max_parallel, so the default 1 applies (orchestrator/gate.py:59).
Find every place a gate subprocess starts (background gate start around daemon.py:1665, the gated_at lease / retry / re-gate path,
the merge-time tests-green run in merge.py if it runs a full gate) and make them all take a slot from one counter keyed by repo root
(count live gate processes from leases plus the background registry). A gate that cannot get a slot waits for the next tick; never
start a second one. Tests (tests/test_gate_timeout.py or tests/test_daemon.py): test_retry_gate_respects_max_parallel,
test_background_and_lease_gates_share_slots, test_merge_tests_count_toward_gate_slots (if merge runs a full gate). Run:
PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests.test_daemon tests.test_gate_timeout. Commit on the task branch.
acceptance: at most [gate].max_parallel gate processes per repo across all start paths

result.summary:
Every gate now takes its slot from one shared count per repo, so no more than `[gate].max_parallel` gates run at once, whichever path starts them. It's committed on `task/T-1750` as `60c8f81`, and `tests.test_daemon` plus `tests.test_gate_timeout` pass: 294 tests, OK.

**Cause:** the daemon only counted its own background gates. `merge.merge` runs the full tests-green gate itself through `gate.run_gate`, and that run was never counted. So when T-0679's gate finished, its merge gate (the gated_at lease path) started while T-0681's background gate started alongside it.

**Fix:**
- **One counter in `gate.py`:** a new `try_acquire_slot` counts slots this process has reserved plus live gate registry entries from other processes, so a CLI merge or another daemon counts too. Registry entries whose process is dead or whose pid was reused don't count.
- **Merge and ship gates:** `run_gate` now waits for a free slot before starting (it checks every 5 s). The only exception is when its caller already holds the slot for that gate.
- **Background gates:** `_start_gate` takes a slot from that counter, and when none is free it returns None with nothing stamped, so the task tries again next tick. The worker thread releases the slot when it finishes.
- **Retries and re-gates:** these go through `_start_gate`, so they are capped the same way.

**Trade-offs:**
- A merge waits for its slot while holding the merge lock. A background gate can also take the slot first, so a merge can sit behind a full 52-minute gate. That respects the cap but is not first-come-first-served.
- Another process's gate only shows up once its subprocess has registered. Two separate processes starting a gate in the same instant could still both start, but the daemon's own threads can't.
- `merge.py` needed no change because `run_gate` handles the wait.

**Files changed:**
- `orchestrator/gate.py` (+79)
- `orchestrator/daemon.py` (+18 / −7)
- `tests/test_daemon.py` (+94): adds `test_retry_gate_respects_max_parallel`, `test_background_and_lease_gates_share_slots` and `test_merge_tests_count_toward_gate_slots`. They use a real blocking gate script, and the last one also covers a gate registered by another process.

**Failures-only output:** none, all green.
result.review: other account, different model; label PR same-family-review
